outcome: Composite adverse neonatal events (low Apgar scores, umbilical artery pH < 7.15, NICU admission, meconium aspiration syndrome, neonatal death)
Cesarean delivery due to fetal distress
Admission to neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: The study included 2142 singleton deliveries at a tertiary university-affiliated hospital, all with meconium-stained amniotic fluid and at least 37 weeks gestation, excluding multiple pregnancies, preterm deliveries, and elective cesarean deliveries.
finding: Secondary meconium-stained amniotic fluid, especially after 40 weeks of gestation, was an independent risk factor for a composite of adverse neonatal outcomes compared to primary meconium-stained amniotic fluid.
mod_finding: Secondary MSAF was associated with significantly higher rates of overall cesarean deliveries, cesarean deliveries due to fetal distress, and other operative deliveries.
